articles.title_original: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
articles.title_zh: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
facts_zh:
Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
- Published
Malaysia's disgraced former Prime Minister Najib Razak has arrived home to begin serving the rest of a jail sentence for corruption under house arrest.
There was a big media presence at his Kuala Lumpur residence to see the 73-year-old return from prison in an SUV late on Tuesday night, escorted by a heavily armed police convoy.
Najib's return ended a four-year prison stint after he was found guilty over the embezzlement of billions of dollars from the country's sovereign wealth fund.

all_titles.en: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions

articles.title_original: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
articles.title_zh: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
facts_zh:
First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
- Published
The first of two days of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi.

While senior officials from Kyiv and Moscow were tight-lipped after the four hour-long discussions, President Volodymyr Zelensky, who was not at the talks, said they had proved "constructive and quite substantive".
Speaking from Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said the meeting had been "very productive".

all_titles.en: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says

articles.title_zh: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
facts_zh:
Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
- Published
French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse.
The Paris prosecutor's office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released.

In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities.

articles.title_zh: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking
facts_zh:
Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking
- Published
Iran has described French accusations that it was behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers as "baseless and hostile".

On Monday, the French authorities blamed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) for the string of hacks, which foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said were "unprecedented" in terms of their scale and "level of aggression".
He added that those responsible would be hit with sanctions.

all_titles.en: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking

articles.title_original: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
articles.title_zh: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
facts_zh:
French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
- Published
One of France's last Resistance heroes from World War Two has died at the age of 104.
Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her future husband, created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters.
After serving as a Resistance courier from 1941, three years later she founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network near the town of Ruillé-sur-Loir.

all_titles.en: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104

articles.title_zh: California police investigate after 27 fall ill at half-marathon running event
facts_zh:
California police investigate after 27 fall ill at half-marathon running event
- Published
Police in Santa Barbara, California, are investigating after nearly 30 people had to seek medical care at a half-marathon running event held in the city on Sunday.

In a statement provided to the BBC's US partner CBS News, officers said they received a report from Santa Barbara Cottage Hospital about race participants who sought medical treatment "for unusual symptoms" after the race ended.
"The cause of the reported symptoms has not been confirmed," the statement added.

all_titles.en: California police investigate after 27 fall ill at half-marathon running event

articles.title_original: US and rest of world must follow China’s lead on green energy, says John Kerry
articles.title_zh: US and rest of world must follow China’s lead on green energy, says John Kerry
facts_zh: Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’ Cop31 live – latest updates China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels , and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.
As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided.
In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”.

articles.title_zh: Police officer dies and another injured after backpack explosion in northern Spain
facts_zh:
Police officer dies and another injured after backpack explosion in northern Spain
- Published
A police officer has died and another has been injured in the northern Spanish city of Oviedo after an explosive device went off at the scene of a shooting.
The blast happened when officers from Spain's canine unit and explosives disposal unit arrived and examined a suspicious backpack following reports of a dispute between neighbours on Tuesday morning.
A woman who had been shot and the injured officer have been taken to hospital for treatment.

all_titles.en: Police officer dies and another injured after backpack explosion in northern Spain

articles.title_original: DR Congo sentences 66 soldiers to death for being 'cowards'
articles.title_zh: DR Congo sentences 66 soldiers to death for being 'cowards'
facts_zh:
DR Congo sentences 66 soldiers to death for being 'cowards'
- Published
At least 66 soldiers have been sentenced to death in the Democratic Republic of Congo for cowardice, mutiny and refusing to obey orders, local media report.
The sentences followed a trial of 71 soldiers before a military court in Walikale, in North Kivu province, in eastern DR Congo.
Four soldiers were acquitted, while another was sentenced to 10 years in prison.

all_titles.en: DR Congo sentences 66 soldiers to death for being 'cowards'

articles.title_zh: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
facts_zh:
Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
- Published
US President Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the affair between the chief executive of Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy.
Trump said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign.
"I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters.
